1.before:
The Documentation Framework is composed of a collection of architectural components.

Each component encapsulates a well-defined architectural responsibility and collaborates with other components through explicit relationships.

Components represent the fundamental building blocks from which the Documentation Framework is constructed.
1.after:
Architectural components are capability boundaries with explicit responsibilities and owner contracts. This document catalogs the 23 capabilities supplied by the working DF architecture and their primary structural allocation; it does not equate a definition, concern, directory or Layer with a component.

Components collaborate through typed relations and scoped required contracts. Architectural definitions establish intended capabilities, not evidence that operational services are implemented or that quality outcomes are guaranteed.

2.after:
The primary responsibility is a component catalog and structural organization: identify the supplied capabilities, preserve their names and primary allocations, delimit responsibility boundaries, type interactions and reference detailed owner specifications.

Family Architecture identifies the documentary area; Type Structure follows this organizational/catalog responsibility. Classification does not follow directory/title alone and does not alter permanent document identity.

3.after:
This source defines capability responsibilities, organization and scoped interaction constraints. Detailed specifications own their domain contracts; this overview neither substitutes for them nor establishes every intended specification as supplied.

DF defines documentary contracts. A DMS, tool or applicable manual process executes management operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. This specification supplies neither an operational permission model nor a deployed workflow/storage implementation.

Every README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md is a non-normalized functional file at every corpus location. Applicable content/reference/integrity checks remain; normalized metadata, Family/Type and document-ID requirements do not apply to those names. This exclusion creates no exceptions to the four Types for normalized documents.

4.before:
The Documentation Framework is organized as a collection of cooperating architectural components.

Conceptually.

```text

                Foundation
                    │

```

Each component performs a specific architectural function.
4.after:
The architecture identifies seven structural areas: Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration. Foundation/Architecture organize supporting definitions; the other five areas allocate capability components. These differ from the five conceptual concerns Knowledge, Documentation, Governance, Discovery and Preservation. Knowledge is subject matter and Preservation is cross-cutting, not additional registered components or structural Layers.

5.before: The Documentation Layer is responsible for representing knowledge.
5.after: Documentation represents Knowledge through descriptive, logical-identity, classification and reusable-structure contracts. Its four capabilities retain separate semantic ownership while contributing to Governance, Discovery and Preservation.

5.1.1.before: Describes documents through standardized descriptive information.
5.1.1.after: Represents structured descriptors for identified documentary entities/editions under applicable owner contracts.

5.1.2.after: Describe documents and support identity, classification, governance and discovery by represented values/references. Document Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain meanings. Dictionary defines descriptors, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Coordinated content/descriptor evolution is permitted; no catalog/Profile or mandatory absent value is invented.

5.2.1.before: Provide a permanent logical identity for every document.
5.2.1.after: Defines stable logical document identity and its applicable allocation/preservation contracts.

5.2.2.after: For normalized documents in scope, distinguish logical domain identity from exact edition, mutable Family/Type, physical location, Status and membership. Adopted corpus DF-SSS-NNN series are stable allocation namespaces independent of current classification; this overview performs no migration or allocation. The functional exclusions in §3 apply before normalized identity obligations. Traceability requires actual identified editions/references, not a guarantee inferred from this purpose.

5.3.1.after: Defines semantic category meaning and applicable documentary assignments.

5.3.2.after: Classify normalized documents using a canonical component or admitted documentary-area Family and exactly one responsibility-based Type from Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference. Optional Class requires an explicit definition. Classification supports governance/discovery without owning their state/approval or search semantics. Mutable classification is distinct from permanent identity, primary component allocation and physical storage; detailed owner reconciliation remains pending.

5.4.1.after: Defines reusable documentary representations and their applicable structural constraints.

5.4.2.after: Standardize structure and support creation through explicit types, schemas, elements, parameters and constraints. A Template definition differs from a concrete document instance. Templates references Metadata, Identity and Classification meanings rather than redefining them; it does not own workflow, policy, Baseline, Registry or storage semantics. Consistency and conformance require actual checks against the applicable contracts, not automatic success from using a template.

6.before: The Governance Layer controls document evolution.
6.after: Governance defines documentary lifecycle, policy, review and immutable snapshot contracts. It does not itself prove an implemented process engine. Exact-edition review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct decisions/events.

6.1.1.after: Defines exact-edition lifecycle, transition, responsibility and evidence contracts.

6.1.2.after: Describe documentary state transitions and publication conditions under applicable Policies. A DMS, tool or manual process executes operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. Logical identity, Version/Revision, exact Status, approval/publication and membership are separate. Illustrative states do not create an unconditional transition graph; older approvals do not approve Draft successors.

6.2.1.after: Defines applicable documentary governance rules and evidence requirements.

6.2.2.after: State review, publication, approval and maintenance policies with applicability and responsible authorities. Rules govern identified editions and operations; actual author contribution, authorization, review, validation and approval remain distinct. Policy definition does not prove implementation, grant an operation automatically or replace semantic owners in other domains.

6.3.1.after: Defines review responsibilities and records examined scope, observations and findings.

6.3.2.after: Technical and architectural review assess exact identified artifacts/rules and consistency within recorded coverage. Reviews may use results from Validation or Consistency Verification, whose executors record applicable checks; overlapping check domains do not create competing semantics or approval authority. A review result is evidence, not an approval, publication decision, Baseline selection or guarantee of product consequences.

6.4.1.after: Defines separately identified immutable selections of exact approved document editions.

6.4.2.after: Preserve explicit selected member identity/edition coordinates and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Approval eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion are separate checks. Release snapshots and historical traceability require scope and selection evidence; a current path or time label alone is insufficient. Draft successors do not retarget older members or inherit membership. This UPDATE creates no Baseline or missing historic approval.

7.before: The Discovery Layer enables knowledge navigation.
7.after: Discovery defines typed connections, catalog/network projections and access to identified entities/editions. Directories remain physical locations rather than semantic authority. Draft, historical and snapshot-specific discovery is allowed with explicit state and scope; discoverability does not confer approval.

7.1.1.before: Maintain the authoritative catalog of architectural entities.
7.1.1.after: Defines catalog/lookup authority for its declared entity/edition scope.

7.1.2.after: Support registration, lookup and discoverability through traceable authoritative source-edition records/projections. Catalog authority does not replace identity, classification, governance or relationship-record meaning. Derived copies retain provenance, refresh and current/stale/historical/snapshot context. Cataloguing does not make Registry an indispensable intermediary for every component or require physical single-copy storage.

7.2.1.after: Defines typed connection records for identified endpoints and their provenance.

7.2.2.after: Map and preserve semantic reference, association, replacement, navigation and required-dependency kinds as applicable. Endpoint domains and identity contracts follow their entity kinds; not every endpoint gets a normalized document ID. Required edges use consumer→provider contract/scope and remain visible, including genuine cycles requiring reconciliation. Explicit records support traceability without fabricating a complete relation catalog.

7.3.1.before: Represent documentation as a semantic network.
7.3.1.after: Defines traceable semantic-network projections of identified entities and typed Relationships records.

7.3.2.after: Support semantic navigation, dependency and impact analysis with authoritative source/edition provenance. Derived values do not acquire competing semantic authority; views declare refresh/freshness and current/historical/snapshot scope. No universal Registry-to-Graph routing or complete network/acyclicity is inferred from this capability.

7.4.1.after: Defines logical access through declared entity/edition and relationship views.

7.4.2.after: Support hierarchical/contextual navigation and cross references with resolvable identified targets, state and relevant freshness context. Sources and relation meanings are explicit; navigation does not automatically impose a provider service dependency, confer approval or replace physical storage contracts.

7.5.1.after: Defines discovery of identified architectural entities through declared indexes/views.

7.5.2.after: Support document, Metadata and semantic search with source-edition provenance and freshness/state limits. Draft and historical results are distinguished from approved/snapshot members. Intended search neither certifies completeness nor requires a universal Registry pipeline or new semantic owner.

8.before: The Automation Layer automates framework activities.
8.after: Automation defines intended repeatable checking/generation capabilities. Applicable implementations consume authoritative owner contracts on identified inputs and provide execution evidence; architectural definitions alone establish neither installed tools nor verified outcomes.

8.1.1.after: Defines scoped evaluation of identified requirements against exact artifacts/editions.

8.1.2.after: Cover Metadata, identity, relationship and consistency requirements supplied by their responsible owners. Actual execution records inputs, rules, checks, observations, coverage, executor and limits. A PASS neither guarantees global correctness nor approves/publishes/selects a Baseline; subsequent changed bytes need their own assessment.

8.2.1.after: Defines generation/completion/synchronization of descriptor representations under applicable owner rules.

8.2.2.after: Identify exact inputs, output edition/representation, applicable Dictionary/Schema/Profile and provenance. Completion derives or requests values through declared rules; it is not permission to invent absent identity, category, lifecycle or approval facts. Generated values require applicable constraint assessment and synchronization/refresh evidence. Capability definition alone proves no implemented generator or successful result.

8.3.1.after: Defines creation/update of scoped Registry projections from authoritative source records/editions.

8.3.2.after: Declare source/input and generated-output provenance, applicable catalog/owner rules and refresh/current-stale handling. Consistency checks state examined records, coverage and limits; generation does not replace domain or relationship-record authority. No implemented synchronization service or automatic complete catalog is inferred.

8.4.1.after: Defines generation of documentary artifacts from identified definitions/inputs.

8.4.2.after: Support table-of-contents, index and navigation artifact generation under applicable representation and owner contracts. Record input/output editions, referenced targets and provenance; verify relevant constraints/references in scope. Generated artifacts are representations, not new semantic authorities or automatically approved publications.

8.5.1.after: Defines scoped cross-record/contract verification under applicable authoritative requirements.

8.5.2.after: Check dependency, relationship and architectural consistency against declared records/editions and actual typed requirements. Record executor, examined scope, observations and limits. Shared check domains with Validation/Reviews do not imply competing rule ownership or global integrity; a partial matrix cannot certify the complete framework graph.

9.before: The Integration Layer connects the Documentation Framework with external systems.
9.after: Integration defines optional use-case adapters to supported external environments and interfaces. Adapters consume owner/authorization contracts without becoming new semantic owners or approvers. Describing integration does not establish its implementation, completeness, performance or mandatory use.

9.1.1.before: Integrate documentation with source control systems.
9.1.1.after: Defines an adapter to supported source-control provenance and versioned representations. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

9.2.1.after: Defines delivery-pipeline adapters executing scoped checks and authorized publication for identified editions. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

9.3.1.after: Defines supported authoring/development adapters under applicable representation and owner contracts. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

9.4.1.after: Defines platform publication adapters following Governance authorization for the exact edition. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

9.5.1.before: Provide semantic reasoning and intelligent assistance.
9.5.1.after: Defines assisted reasoning/authoring against identified domain contracts and source evidence. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred. AI assistance does not acquire domain-semantic or approval authority. Actual contribution and examined bytes are recorded separately from user authorization; later human/tool edits require resulting-byte assessment without inherited results or product-consequence responsibility.

11.before: Every architectural component shall possess the following characteristics.
11.after: The following characteristics guide design and assessment within applicable contracts. They are objectives and structural constraints, not evidence of achieved operational quality.

11.1.before: Each component shall have one clearly defined responsibility.
11.1.after: Each capability has a defined primary responsibility, semantic owner and allocation. Related support roles may span concerns through explicit contracts without assigning another competing primary owner. Assess cohesion against detailed responsibilities rather than directory uniformity.

11.2.before: Interactions between components shall be explicitly defined.
11.2.after: Required interactions identify consumer, provider, authoritative source edition, required contract and scope. Association/navigation references remain separately typed. Implementations identify input/output representations, executor and evidence; this overview does not manufacture missing detailed interfaces.

11.3.before: Components shall evolve independently whenever possible.
11.3.after: Preserve separation and compatible provider contracts where feasible. Required consumption, cross-cutting participation and coordinated content/descriptor changes may couple editions or releases; modularity does not guarantee unconditional independent evolution.

11.4.before: Components shall be reusable by multiple architectural services.
11.4.after: Reuse follows applicable owner contracts, scope and constraints. Intended reuse across services/components does not prove universal suitability, unrestricted scale or an implemented reusable service.

11.5.before: Components shall support future extensions without compromising existing functionality.
11.5.after: New capabilities or changed interfaces require demonstrated need, primary allocation, owner/consumer impact mapping, dependency assessment and transition evidence. Extension can affect existing meaning/functionality; necessary incompatible changes are explicitly justified and versioned under §15.

11.6.before: Components shall remain independent from implementation technologies.
11.6.after: Definitions avoid prescribing implementation technology unless it is an explicit integration constraint. Actual tools still require formats, storage adapters and execution evidence. Technology independence does not establish tool availability or universal compatibility.

```text

```

Dependencies shall always follow the layered architecture defined in **DF-ARC-004 — Architectural Layers**.

Circular dependencies between components are prohibited.
12.after:
A required dependency is directed **consumer→provider** and identifies the provider contract needed in a declared scope. Documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are distinct meanings; visual position does not identify required edges.

Apply Layers V2.0 R1 §§12–13: support order is Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation, Integration. A required cross-Layer provider precedes its consumer in that declared order; lower/higher means support precedence, not page position. Same-Layer contracts require explicit interfaces/ownership and cycle assessment. The rule does not require every earlier-area provider or an adjacent serial service chain; changing the constraint requires an assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary upward exception.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | Discovery | Metadata | Documentation | Descriptive values with source-edition provenance | When indexing edition descriptors; refresh or identify stale values |

These seven selected contracts preserve Concepts V2.0 R1 §8 and Layers V2.0 R1 §12, consistent with Blueprint §8.11. Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies are same-Layer requirements. They are scoped architectural declarations, not a verified complete graph, implementation inventory or execution sequence.

Circular required dependencies between components, within/across areas, are prohibited in the governed contract scope. Assess actual edges and owner/consumer evidence. A genuine indispensable contract/cycle must remain visible and be reconciled; do not conceal it by changing a relationship label.          Integration Components


applied_map.before: Type=Components is outside the four adopted Types. The primary purpose identifies a component catalog, organization and responsibility boundaries; Family Architecture denotes the documentary area. Header V1.0 R0 Draft/Baseline1.0 and absent Author are declarations, not approval/selection evidence.
applied_map.proposal: Use Architecture/Structure according to the primary catalog/organization responsibility. Retain DF-ARC-005/path, omit invented Component/Class and preserve received declarations/absent Author in history. Record actual working contribution separately from authorization, review, validation and approval. Assess a Draft/unassigned successor with monotonically incremented Revision against actual normative changes.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Header/classification rationale/history conform to the four-Type policy, stable identity and actual contribution. No inherited approval, Baseline or responsibility for later changed bytes is implied.
applied_map.after: Architecture/Structure V2.0 R1 Draft/unassigned; received Components/R0/Baseline1.0 and absent Author retained, actual Codex contribution separate; ID/path stable, no Component/Class invented.

applied_map.before: §§5–9 define 23 named capabilities in 4/4/5/5/5 areas, agreeing with Layers. §4 mixes Foundation/Architecture support areas and capability groupings; §10 ends with Automation as though it were another component, although it is the grouping of five capabilities. The source does not distinguish register, structural area, conceptual concern and cross-cutting participation.
applied_map.proposal: Provide an explicit 23-entry primary-allocation register preserving every canonical name and original component section. Distinguish seven structural areas and five concerns, with Foundation/Architecture as support definitions and Automation as an area rather than a 24th component. Exactly one primary allocation allows explicit participation across concerns. Preserve Metadata in Documentation and Workflow/Baselines in Governance; no Knowledge/Preservation component or Layer is invented.
applied_map.closure_criterion: All 23 entries occur once in the register with 4/4/5/5/5 allocation and stable names; all three views distinguish entity/capability/area meanings. No extra or relocated component is inferred from a concern, directory or diagram label.
applied_map.after: Explicit 23-row component register with original section/primary area, seven structural areas versus five conceptual concerns and supporting definitions. Automation is an area, not a 24th capability; all names/4/4/5/5/5 allocations preserved.

applied_map.before: Three unnamed views are untyped chains. §10 claims every relationship is explicitly defined without providing kinds/contracts. §12 asserts a dependency hierarchy and refers to Layers, whose corrected support-order constraint and same-Layer contracts are not represented by this chain.
applied_map.proposal: Replace §4 with allocation meaning, §10 with typed associations/ownership/projection relations and §12 with scoped required consumer→provider contracts. Preserve the seven intended Concepts/Layers pairs with contract, scope and primary allocation, including Workflow→Policies and Knowledge Graph→Relationships. Apply the declared support order only to required cross-Layer providers. Separate documentary authority, semantic connection, projection, navigation and execution; preserve actual required cycles visibly and retain the prohibition. Do not invent additional mandatory edges, arbitrary upward exceptions or a complete graph from a visual chain.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Each view and new assertion states its meaning; every required edge has consumer/provider, contract/scope and source edition. Genuine requirements and cycles are not concealed by labels. No global acyclicity or consumer conformity is claimed.
applied_map.after: Three original-section views separate allocation, typed associations and scoped required consumption. Seven contracts exactly preserve Layers/Concepts with same-Layer pairs; support-order constraint/cycle prohibition explicit, no invented full graph or hidden required edge.

applied_map.before: Metadata supports identity/classification/governance/discovery without owner distinctions, Identity applies to every document and Templates ensures consistency. Classification is generic; identity, mutable classification and exact edition are not distinguished. Normalization applicability and functional exclusions are absent.
applied_map.proposal: Scope normalized obligations and exclude README.md/CHANGELOG.md/ArchitecturalMilestones.md at every location while retaining content/reference checks. Metadata represents descriptors; Identity/Classification/Governance own meanings. Dictionary defines, Schema references/organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Distinguish stable logical identity from edition, Status, classification and membership; adopted Family/Type and allocation-series identity remain independent. Templates defines reusable representation under applicable constraints, without automatic consistency or owner-semantic takeover.
applied_map.closure_criterion: §5 responsibilities retain their intended support roles with explicit domain ownership and applicability, no invented catalog/Profile or mandatory normalized identity for functional files. Representation, logical identity, edition and classification remain distinct; no path/ID migration is inferred.
applied_map.related_records: INV-02 remains Not applicable; REV2-03/04/06/07/08; ARC003-03/04; ARC004-04
applied_map.after: Functional exclusions apply before normalized obligations. Metadata representation distinct from Identity/Classification/Governance meaning; Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance under one effective Profile. Identity/edition/classification/membership and Template definition/instance separated; no catalog, profile or migration fabricated.

applied_map.before: Governance controls evolution and Workflow manages lifecycle/publication without definition-versus-execution or exact-edition gates. Reviews and automation both verify consistency without result/authority separation. Baselines preserves versions/release snapshots but does not specify exact member selection or approval eligibility.
applied_map.proposal: Define Workflow/Policies/Reviews/Baselines as documentary contract capabilities; DMS/tool/manual execution and CMS change governance remain separate. Review/validation/approval/publication/membership are distinct events for exact editions. Baseline independently identified immutable explicit exact approved-edition selection with relevant pinned context/evidence; eligibility, consistency and inclusion separate. Reviews records findings/evidence, Validation executes/evidences identified checks and Consistency Verification covers declared cross-record contracts; overlapping checks do not grant competing semantics or approval. Publication adapters consume Governance authorization.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Governance/verification/executor boundaries and exact-edition snapshot gates are explicit; no successful check or adapter automatically approves, publishes, selects membership or retargets earlier editions.
applied_map.after: Documentary lifecycle/policy/review/snapshot contracts distinct from DMS/tool/manual execution and CMS scope. Exact immutable approved-edition selection and pinned context, eligibility/consistency/inclusion separate. Review/check/approval/publication distinct; verification domains do not create competing semantics.

applied_map.before: Registry is authoritative catalog without domain/projection limits; Relationships purpose is restricted to architectural dependencies, while Navigation and Graph also require semantic associations/references. Projections, records, freshness and endpoint ownership are not distinguished.
applied_map.proposal: Relationships owns typed records with endpoint identity and provenance, including semantic/reference/association/replacement/navigation/required kinds. Registry catalog authority and Graph network views reference exact authoritative sources/editions; derived copies retain refresh/current-stale context without competing domain authority. Navigation/Search consume declared sources and may expose Draft/historical editions with state. Do not impose universal Registry→Graph routing, physical single-copy storage or required runtime edges from every semantic relation.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Discovery capability boundaries distinguish authoritative records from traceable projections and consumers; relationships are not restricted to dependencies or used to hide actual required edges. No unverified pipeline, completeness or global consistency is asserted.
applied_map.after: Relationships owns typed records; Registry/Graph traceable projections with refresh/state/provenance; Navigation/Search consumers. Draft discovery qualified, no universal pipeline, domain-authority transfer or semantic/required-edge conflation.

applied_map.before: Generators generate, complete and synchronize Metadata/Registry; Validation verifies compliance and Consistency Verification verifies integrity without rules, exact-input scope or execution evidence. §16 says detailed specifications collectively define complete operational behavior.
applied_map.proposal: Define intended Automation contracts separately from implemented executors. Generators consume authoritative descriptor/identity/classification/governance/relationship rules and identify input/output editions, provenance and applicable constraints; completion is not permission to invent absent values or semantics. Registry generation produces scoped traceable projections with refresh/stale handling. Validation/Consistency Verification declare exact artifacts, applicable rules, coverage, observations, limits and executor. Capability definitions alone establish neither implemented tools nor whole-framework correctness, approval or product outcomes.
applied_map.closure_criterion: All five Automation responsibilities have explicit owner-contract/executor/evidence limits, retaining intended generation/check domains without manufactured values, semantic authority, automatic conformity or a deployed implementation claim.
applied_map.after: Generation/completion/synchronization consumes owner rules with exact input/output and provenance, without inventing absent values/semantics. Validation/Consistency Verification require scoped checks/executor evidence; no implemented-tool, global conformity or product guarantee.

applied_map.before: CI/CD automates validation/publication, platform integration publishes and AI provides semantic reasoning without authorization, authority or implementation boundaries. Components are described as implementing the framework and operational building blocks without supplied execution evidence.
applied_map.proposal: Define optional use-case adapters to supported external environments/interfaces. Source control supports provenance; CI/CD executes scoped checks and authorized publication; IDE supports authoring; platform publishing follows exact-edition Governance authorization. AI assistance references responsible domain semantics and records actual contribution/evidence separately from user authorization/approval. No external integration becomes a new semantic owner or implies an implemented service, guaranteed outcome or responsibility for subsequently modified bytes.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Five Integration roles retain canonical names/allocation and state applicable contract/authorization/executor limits. No automatic publication, new approval authority, mandatory ecosystem or unsupported implementation evidence remains.
applied_map.after: Optional supported external adapters with contract/authorization/executor boundaries. Source-control provenance, CI/CD checks, authoring and platform publication retain roles; AI references domain semantics and actual attribution, no new owner/approver or inherited result after later edits.

applied_map.before: Single responsibility, independence, reusable services, harmless extension and achieved modularity/maintainability are stated as general requirements or outcomes. Evolution assumes independence without assessing provider/consumer contracts; Principles allows justified breaking changes.
applied_map.proposal: Express cohesion, reuse, separation and technology independence as assessed objectives with scope/implementation limits. A new capability requires demonstrated need, primary allocation, owner/consumer contract mapping and transition evidence; extension may affect existing functionality. Preserve compatibility where feasible and explicitly justify/version necessary incompatibility under policy. Do not guarantee independent editions/releases, harmless extensions or complete operational quality.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Characteristics/evolution/conclusion use bounded claims and a concrete compatibility/impact path; no architecture-free extension or automatic quality/independence guarantee remains.
applied_map.after: Characteristics and quality are assessed objectives; extension can affect owners/consumers. New capability/allocation/contract changes need previous/new mapping and transition; actual V2.0 incompatible reconciliation justified, Revision monotonic.

applied_map.before: §13 lists eight generic specification roles without operational links, including five exact specification titles not declared in the supplied corpus. §14 uses five plain Architecture IDs and §16 implies complete operational behavior. Four actual detailed Documentation specifications are supplied; no local history/input/view provenance is recorded.
applied_map.proposal: Map component to actual supplied source or explicitly conceptual/planned specification responsibility; add real paths/IDs for Metadata, Identity, Classification and Templates without treating an illustrative eight-row list as exhaustive. Qualify Workflow/Registry/Relationships/Graph/Validation roles: no dedicated source with those exact titles was found, which is not proof that external specifications cannot exist. Link five Architecture roles plus applicable Foundation/review owners, record input/local history and all three original view texts/hashes. Preserve historic pending events; source presence is not approval, implementation or completed peer review.
applied_map.closure_criterion: Every operational reference resolves to an intended supplied identity; illustrative/unsupplied roles and partial comparison limits are explicit. Numbering/input/history/view provenance traceable without invented specification IDs, historic authors or completed peer cycles.
applied_map.after: Fourteen links resolve to five Architecture, three Foundation, four actual detailed specs and review policy/report. Five generic specs qualified as intended roles with bounded title-scan limit; all original numbering/three view texts/hashes/input/history preserved.
